item.title: index
item.description: India 18th Century–Present From the late Mughal order through Company sovereignty, Crown rule, and the political settlements of the twentieth century, India sat at the meeting of its own long civilizational continuum and the institutions, techniques, and ideas that arrived with European sea power.

item.title: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad — India Wins Freedom (complete version)
item.description: Autobiographical narrative of the transfer of power, 1937–48, dictated to Humayun Kabir: Congress ministries, wartime presidency, Cripps, Quit India, Ahmednagar jail, Simla, Cabinet Mission, Interim Government, Mountbatten, and partition. Orient Blackswan complete edition restores passages sealed until 1988.

item.title: B. R. Ambedkar — Pakistan or the Partition of India (2nd ed. / AMS 1975)
item.description: Wartime treatise on the Muslim League’s Pakistan demand: Muslim case (nation, home, escape from degradation), Hindu objections (unity, defence, communal peace), alternatives (Hardayal; guessed Muslim parity scheme), Turkey and Czechoslovakia as lessons, the Hindu–Muslim malaise (stagnation, aggression), and Ambedkar’s own Part V (must there be Pakistan; problems of partition; who can decide). AMS Press 1975 NY reprint of the 2nd edition (preface 1 Jan. 1945).

item.title: W. Nassau Lees — Indian Musalmáns (1871)
item.description: Three Times letters (Oct–Nov 1871) after Justice Norman’s assassination, on Muslim loyalty, discontent, and redress; plus a Prince Consort education essay, four Calcutta Englishman articles on Oriental vs English schooling, Lord Mayo’s 1871 education resolution, and Macaulay’s 1835 Minute as appendix. Not Hunter’s same-year pamphlet despite ZIP metadata.

item.title: Sir Richard Temple — India in 1880 (3rd ed., 1881)
item.description: Contemporary survey of the Indian empire at the turn into Ripon’s viceroyalty: geography and art, Europeans and Native States, material and moral progress, education and missions, law and crime, land and revenues, canals/railways/roads, products and commerce, sanitation and famine, science and sport, navy/army/foreign relations (Russia, Afghanistan), finance. Third edition, Murray 1881.

item.title: H. H. Wilson — The History of British India, Vol. IX (continuation, 1848)
item.description: Volume IX of the nine-volume Madden set: Wilson’s Volume III / Book III, 1823–1835 — Adam and Amherst, first Burma war (Rangoon, Ramoo, Barrackpore, Donabew, Yandabo), Bhurtpore, Bentinck (half-batta, opium, suttee, thugs, English education), Coorg and Mysore, native states and non-interference, 1833 charter ending Company trade. Completes Wilson 1805–1835.

item.title: H. H. Wilson — The History of British India, Vol. VIII (continuation, 1846)
item.description: Volume VIII of the Madden set (half-title now ‘in nine volumes’): Wilson’s Book II chs I–XII, 1813–1823, administration of the Marquis of Hastings — Nepal war, Kandy, Pindaris, last Maratha war (Kirki, Sitabaldi, Mahidpur, Peshwa deposed), Central India settlement, courts/revenue/press. Complete as Vol. VIII; 1823–1835 remains later.

item.title: Lucien Wolf — Life of the First Marquess of Ripon, Vol. II (1921)
item.description: Volume II of two: Indian Viceroyalty 1880–84 (Afghanistan, Kandahar, army, Baring, local self-government, Vernacular Press Act, Ilbert Bill) then elder statesman (Home Rule, Admiralty, Colonial Office, Liberal leadership, 1906 Education Bill, Morley reforms) to death 1909. Completes the Life.

item.title: Lucien Wolf — Life of the First Marquess of Ripon, Vol. I (1921)
item.description: Volume I of two: George Frederick Samuel Robinson from birth in Downing Street (1827) through Commons, War Office, Cabinet, Lord President, Alabama claims, conversion to Rome, and Gladstone’s choice of a Catholic Viceroy (1880). Indian apprenticeship 1857–58; the viceroyalty itself is Vol. II.

item.title: H. H. Wilson — The History of British India, Vol. VII (continuation, 1845)
item.description: Volume VII of the eight-volume Madden set: Wilson’s continuation from 1805, Book I chs I–VIII (peace with the Marathas to the 1813 charter) — Barlow, Vellore, Minto, Travancore and the Madras officers’ mutiny, Java and Mauritius, dakoiti and revenue, 1813 charter and missionaries. Complete as Vol. VII; Wilson continues in Vol. VIII.
